correctness.rationale: On the invariant x=y=0 axis, b=2/h gives z→-z and every A>0 a least-period-two orbit. Along its two points the 3D return splits into eigenvalue +1 and P(A)=M(-A)M(A). Direct multiplication proves tr P=T=tr(M0²), det P=m²-h^4a²A². For a>2c>0, Schur inequalities make M0 and M0² stable for all sufficiently small h and 0<T<2. The three degree-two Schur inequalities then give exactly two positive and strictly ordered amplitudes A+ and A−, with 0,1,2 strictly expanding transverse multipliers in the successive open intervals. A suitable contracting norm at any A in (0,A+) controls transverse iterates, while the exact quadratic axial drift is summable, proving an open set converges geometrically to some period-two orbit. Exact factorization of det(I-M0²) yields A+~2sqrt(a(a−2c))/(ah), while A−~2/(ah²). Symbolic package checker rederives both invariants and rational benchmark. No assertion about the nonlinear dynamics at either wall.

value.rationale: The axial z-update of this standard forward-Euler Chen discretization becomes an exact flip at the natural scalar stability limit hb=2, so persistent periodic dynamics is a motivated (not arbitrary) modeling issue. A single resonance supports uncountably many nonzero cycles; these partition sharply into 0,1,2 expanding transverse modes at two explicit widely separated h-dependent amplitudes. A full-dimensional open tube converges to selected cycles rather than to a specific isolated attractor. This resolves a concrete gap beyond fixed-point studies, distinguishes discretization-induced oscillations from the single continuous equilibrium, and offers parameter-uniform analytic benchmarks. Applicability limited to resonant Euler steps and a>2c>0.
